newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.4 pct in Oct -- Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.4 pct in Oct -- Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.4 percent in the first three weeks of fiscal October versus September, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index.

The index rose 7.3 percent when compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales rose 6.6 percent in the week ended October 26, compared with the same week a year ago, it said.

Retailers noted strength in Halloween-related merchandise, but indicated that the higher sales momentum this month is really being driven by apparel and accessories, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.
"Chain stores are above plan for the month and department stores are about on plan for the month," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Regionally, California and the west continue to report the largest sales gains, he said.
Eilenberg also noted that women, who are currently replacing their wardrobes, have been contributing to the recent rise in the apparel market.
